name: oauth.access
purpose: Exchanges a temporary OAuth verifier code for an access token.

client_id.desc: Issued when you created your application. If possible, avoid sending client_id and client_secret as parameters in your request and instead supply the Client ID and Client Secret using the HTTP Basic authentication scheme.

client_secret.desc: Issued when you created your application. If possible, avoid sending client_id and client_secret as parameters in your request and instead supply the Client ID and Client Secret using the HTTP Basic authentication scheme.

code.desc: The code param returned via the OAuth callback.

redirect_uri.desc: This must match the originally submitted URI (if one was sent).

single_channel.desc: Request the user to add your app only to a single channel. Only valid with a legacy workspace app.

safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true. 'existence-only' verified does NOT mean 'safe to call' -- it only means the method name is real.
